reviews.review_title: Rinse before outdoor use to prevent color bleeding!
reviews.review_text: I bought these to add some festive beauty around the door outside my condo complex. The neighbors love it as much as I do. Exactly what I wanted in a garland, definitely looks best with two strands together side by side if you want a more thick/full look, but they seemed pretty good as a single strand as well, depending on what you are looking for. The colors are great and I love that there are such a variety so they look more realistic. I shook them all around in multiple ways and I did not have any leaves ever fall off so the quality seems great. The only reason I deducted one star is because, as other reviewers have mentioned, I had to do the extra steps of taking each strand and running it under cold water in my tub to remove excess color so that it would not bleed when it rains outside. I guess that only matters if you plan to use this outside. I took each strand and ran it under the cold tap in the tub and agitated it around a bit and then use my handheld showerhead to ensure there was no more dye. There was not as much color coming off as I expected based on the reviews but I assume it is because other people filled the tub with water and then soaked all of them together, which I did not do. After a quick rinse, I put them in a large garment bag and put them in the dryer on the gentle/low heat cycle for about 20 minutes.

reviews.review_text: These maple leaf garlands were a fun and affordable way to decorate for fall. The leaves are obviously artificial when viewed up close, but once displayed, they looked festive and added great color to my home.I used them in several different areas, including above windows and around my fireplace. The garlands were easy to shape and arrange, and I was able to tuck the ends behind other decorations so they blended in nicely.The leaves have a nice mix of fall colors, and the strands were full enough to make an impact without needing a lot of extra decorating. I used them in several different areas of my home, which made them very versatile. The colors were bright and vibrant and showed up well both during the day and with decorative lighting at night. They also arrived without any strong chemical or plastic smell, which I appreciated. Overall, I was very happy with how they looked and would use them again for seasonal decorating.

reviews.review_text: Firstly, most of the product pictures are AI, and look nothing like the actual ghosts.The sheets are AWFUL:1, They're jagged and uneven so no matter what the tripod will be visible on at least one side2, They're so thin so you can see the ball and tripod through them3, There's not even a way to secure the sheet to the base underneath, as if it won't fall off loosely draped over a plastic ball?4, There's a nasty film on them that made my hands feel disgustingNow for the base parts:The fairy lights- there's not really a way to make them look good because it's just a bunch of separate little light spots inside the head. The instructions are bare minimum, no pictures or steps, I just had to figure it out myself. And lastly, the tripod is held together by plastic nobs and closures, I felt like I was breaking it every time I adjusted the height- but hey, it comes with stakes at least, that's SOMETHING.Now for accessories: The eyes and mouth are literally just foam stickers.... stickers don't stick well to fabric- I highly doubt they'd last long. The witch hats come with one safety pin each, like that'll keep the whole thing together. Yes, I'm sure most people have extra pins lying around, but for $30 I expect the product to be self-sufficient.The whole thing overall is sooooo flimsy and weak, I find it hilarious they think it would survive outside- one gust of wind and these ghosts would be a pile on the ground. Maybe worth 10 bucks max, anyone could make their own ghosts way better for cheaper.

reviews.review_title: Soft, cute, well made — I’d buy more
reviews.review_text: These are even cuter in person. They arrived clean and protected in a resealable zip-top bag, which I really liked. You don’t have to cut the packaging open, so I’m keeping the bags to store the covers in after Halloween.Right out of the package they were extremely soft. There was a very subtle new-fabric smell, but nothing strong or unpleasant. The raised ghosts are actually fluffy and dimensional, rather than just being a printed design, and the black embroidered faces give them a really cute 3D look. The back has a smooth, almost suede-like feel.The covers feel sturdy and the stitching looks good. The zipper is small and discreet, so you really don’t notice it when it’s closed. Looking at the inside, I did notice a few loose ends from the black embroidery, but they don’t affect the appearance from the outside.One thing I wish they had included is a care-instruction tag. There isn’t one sewn into the covers, so you’ll need to refer back to the listing, which says to machine wash cold on gentle and tumble dry low.I also agree with the listing’s “spooky neutral” description. They’re Halloween-themed without being bright or overly cartoonish, so they’re easy to work into regular home decor. The listing mentions using them on a porch, but personally I wouldn’t. The white plush material and embroidery feel much better suited to indoor use, especially if you want to keep them looking nice.I bought the 18x18 set of two, and I would absolutely buy more for my other throw pillows. I especially like that there are different sizes and colors available, so I can mix and match while keeping the same ghost theme.For the price I paid, I’m very happy with the quality. Cute, ridiculously soft, and exactly the kind of Halloween decor I was looking for. 👻

We spent hours together making different turkey characters, and she was so proud of her creations. She made turkeys for all her grandparents and even decorated placecards for our Thanksgiving table. The stickers sparked her creativity and kept her entertained for a long time, which as a parent is priceless! The set provided great value with plenty of stickers for multiple craft sessions. It was a wonderful hands-on activity that got her excited about the holiday. She loved mixing and matching the different features to give each turkey its own personality. These stickers are perfect for Thanksgiving crafts, classroom activities, or just creative play. My daughter asks to use them constantly and has already requested more craft sticker sets. Highly recommend for any parent looking for engaging, creative activities!

reviews.review_title: Spooky purple solar lights - perfect for Halloween
reviews.review_text: Halloween is my absolute favorite holiday to decorate for, and these purple solar torch lights are the perfect addition to my outdoor decorations! I love flickering flame lights because they create such a fun, spooky atmosphere, and the purple glow on these gives my yard an extra eerie Halloween vibe. They’re a great way to add some color and ambiance along walkways, in the garden, or around the porch without having to worry about real flames. I also love that they’re solar-powered, so there are no cords to deal with or outlets needed. Simply assemble them, place them somewhere they can get plenty of sunlight, and let them automatically light up when it gets dark.Another thing I appreciate is how easy these lights are to set up and incorporate into my Halloween display. The flickering effect adds a fun, flame-like appearance that makes the yard feel a little more haunted, especially when combined with other Halloween decorations. Since they’re designed for outdoor use and are waterproof, they’re a convenient option for seasonal decorating without having to bring them inside every time the weather changes. The solar power is an added bonus because there’s no need to keep buying batteries or worry about running electrical cords across the yard. If you love Halloween as much as I do and want to add a spooky purple glow to your outdoor decorations, these solar torch lights are a fun and festive choice!

reviews.review_text: As someone who looks forward to the LEGO advent calendars every year, the 2026 LEGO City Advent Calendar (Set 60510) is an absolute home run. From the mini toy workbench and Christmas train to the mail station for letters to Santa, everything feels cinematic and useful.• Box Converts into a Playmat: The front flap folds down into a gorgeous illustration of Santa’s Workshop. Instead of the micro-builds cluttering up your counters, kids have a built-in backdrop to play out stories as they open a new door each morning.A Quick Tip for Parents: Because this set features a rare volume of the entire Claus family and their workshop crew in an affordable box, it is a massive hit with Adult Fans of LEGO (AFOLs) building winter villages. Grab it early on Amazon before the November/December price spikes!Final Verdict:With easy-to-follow instructions printed right inside the doors, it’s perfect for independent building for kids ages 5+. It's a time to gather with family, reconnect with friends, and create memories around the table. While the menu is important, the table itself sets the tone for the entire celebration. In 2026, Thanksgiving decorating is moving away from overly themed displays and embracing a more refined, timeless style. Homeowners are choosing natural materials, warm color palettes, and handcrafted pieces that feel inviting, elegant, and meaningful. Whether you're hosting your first Thanksgiving dinner or continuing a family tradition, these decorating trends will help you create a table your guests will remember long after dessert is served. --- # Trend #1: Natural Woven Textures Take Center Stage Natural materials continue to dominate home décor, and Thanksgiving is the perfect season to embrace them. Handwoven placemats, baskets, trays, and candle holders add warmth and texture that beautifully complement the rich colors of autumn. Instead of relying on disposable decorations, many hosts are investing in handcrafted pieces they can enjoy year after year. Natural woven décor pairs effortlessly with pumpkins, candles, seasonal greenery, and heirloom dinnerware, creating a timeless look that never feels trendy. Mix: * Taper candles * Pillar candles * Hurricane lanterns * Tea lights The soft glow encourages guests to relax, linger, and enjoy the evening together. # Trend #7: Mix Family Heirlooms with New Pieces One of the most beautiful decorating trends is blending old and new. In modern holiday design, thanksgiving table runners act as the visual anchor for the feast. They provide an intentional path for the eye to follow, grounding your centerpieces, vases, and serving platters. This structural element helps resolve the common "curated vs. cluttered" debate. Instead of decor items floating aimlessly across a vast table, a runner creates a dedicated zone for your creative expression. It adds vital texture and warmth without overwhelming the room. You want a sophisticated atmosphere that still feels approachable. A runner achieves this balance perfectly by softening hard surfaces while offering practical protection against heat and unexpected spills. ### Why Choose a Runner Over a Full Tablecloth? If you've invested in a beautiful walnut, oak, or quartz dining table, don't feel obligated to hide it. A runner allows the natural grain and character of your furniture to shine. This creates a modern, less formal environment compared to traditional, heavy tablecloths. It's a style choice that feels fresh, airy, and intentional. Beyond the aesthetics, the logistics are far more manageable for a busy host. High-quality thanksgiving table runners are easier to launder, press, and store than bulky, large-scale linens. This efficiency is a game changer when you're managing a complex holiday schedule and want to focus on your guests rather than your laundry room. ### Setting the Mood for Your 2026 Gathering Your choice of fabric and color sets the psychological stage for the day. A crisp, neutral runner signals a clean, minimalist aesthetic, while a heavy weave suggests a rustic and cozy vibe. For 2026, we see a distinct move toward premium materials like linen that offer a timeless, artisanal feel. This shifts the energy from a casual family lunch to an elegant evening celebration. It's the simplest way to elevate your hosting experience while maintaining a sense of curated simplicity. ## Selecting Premium Materials: Linen, Cotton, and Beyond The tactile quality of your table setting determines how guests feel the moment they sit down. While budget synthetic options might look acceptable in a package, they often lack the substantial weight and graceful "drape" required for a professional look. Premium thanksgiving table runners should feel substantial to the touch and hang with a purposeful, heavy elegance over the table edge. This weight ensures the fabric stays in place throughout the meal, even as platters are passed and glasses are refilled. ### The Timeless Appeal of Linen Runners Linen remains the gold standard for a reason. It offers a unique, slubbed texture that catches the warm flicker of candlelight in a way that flat, man-made fibers simply cannot. This material is incredibly durable. A high-quality linen piece is a multi-year investment that actually softens and improves with every wash. If you're looking for that perfect blend of rustic charm and high-end sophistication, linen is your best ally. It brings an organic, worldly feel to the dining room that resonates with the spirit of the season. Its natural breathability and strength mean it won't pill or thin out over time, unlike cheaper alternatives. ### Cotton and Blends for Versatile Style High-density cotton is an excellent choice for hosts who prefer a crisp, tailored appearance. It provides a smooth surface that acts as a clean backdrop for intricate flatware or colorful centerpieces. Look for weaves that offer a subtle sheen under your dining room lighting. This adds a layer of quiet luxury without being overly reflective. Many cotton thanksgiving table runners feature delicate embroidered details, adding a touch of seasonal craftsmanship that feels personal and warm. These blends often offer a bit more structure, which is ideal if you want sharp, clean lines at the end of your table. Maintenance shouldn't be a deterrent to choosing quality. Modern holiday hosting is about ease. Many premium linens are designed to be machine-washed and look stunning with their natural, soft-washed texture. You don't always need a perfectly pressed surface to achieve a sophisticated look. Often, the slight, natural undulations of real fabric add to the welcoming, lived-in atmosphere of a family gathering. If you are ready to elevate your holiday aesthetic, explore our curated collection of runners to find your perfect match. ## Mastering Proportions: Sizing Your Runner for Any Table Scale is the silent partner in great design. If your runner is too short, it looks like an afterthought. If it's too long, it becomes a tripping hazard or crowds the guest's lap. For a classic, professional look, aim for an overhang of 6 to 10 inches on each side. This provides enough fabric to signal luxury without interfering with seating comfort. It's a small detail that makes a massive impact on the overall symmetry of your room. Measure your table length carefully before you start shopping. Add 12 to 20 inches to that total to find your ideal runner length. If you're leaning toward a contemporary aesthetic, consider the "short runner" trend. In this style, the fabric stops about 4 inches before the table edge on both sides. This centered look keeps the focus entirely on your centerpiece and works beautifully on modern, minimalist surfaces. It's a clean approach that highlights the craftsmanship of your table while providing a crisp foundation for thanksgiving table runners. ### Styling Round and Square Tables Square and round tables often baffle hosts who are used to rectangular layouts. A single runner can sometimes feel visually thin in these spaces. Try the "X" technique instead. Place two identical runners perpendicular to each other to create a cross shape. This anchors the center of the table while providing a balanced backdrop for every guest's place setting. For a small round table, one centered runner can actually elongate the room by drawing the eye across the diameter. It's a simple yet effective trick for Mastering the Art of Stunning Table Scapes in tighter quarters. Focus on maintaining visual balance by keeping your centerpiece low and contained within the runner's width. ### Proportions for Large Family Gatherings Thanksgiving often means adding every available leaf to the dining table. If your table expands, your linens must follow suit. For extra-long banquet tables, don't stress about finding a single, impossible 20-foot piece. Instead, overlap two identical thanksgiving table runners. You can easily hide the seam under a substantial floral arrangement or a lush greenery garland. Width also plays a critical role in guest comfort. A standard runner is usually 12 to 14 inches wide. Ensure your choice leaves at least 15 inches of clear space on either side for dinner plates, flatware, and glassware. This prevents the fabric from tangling with place settings and keeps the layout feeling organized and airy. Enjoy the art of gathering with confidence and ease. ## Frequently Asked Questions ### Should a Thanksgiving table runner hang over the edge? Your runner should ideally hang 6 to 10 inches over each edge of your table. This length provides a balanced, professional look that doesn't interfere with your guests' seating comfort. If you prefer a contemporary feel, choose a shorter runner that ends just before the table edge. This centered style highlights your table's material while anchoring your holiday centerpiece. Always measure your table length before purchasing to ensure a perfect, tailored fit. ### Can I use a table runner on a round table for Thanksgiving? Absolutely use a table runner on a round table to create visual interest. A single runner centered across the diameter provides a clean foundation for a floral centerpiece. For a more formal look, place two runners perpendicularly to anchor the table's center. This technique works well for smaller dining areas where you want to maximize the impact of your thanksgiving table runners without crowding the surface. It adds a layer of curated sophistication. ### What is the best fabric for a holiday table runner? Linen is the gold standard for holiday runners due to its durability and natural texture. It offers a sophisticated, matte finish that catches candlelight beautifully, creating a warm and inviting atmosphere. While high-density cotton provides a crisp, clean look, linen actually improves with every wash and lasts for years. Its substantial weight ensures the fabric drapes elegantly over the table edge, signaling a high-end, curated experience for your family and guests. ### How wide should a table runner be for a standard dining table? A standard runner is typically 12 to 14 inches wide for most dining tables. This width provides enough room for centerpieces and candles while leaving at least 15 inches of space on either side for place settings. You don't want a runner that's too wide, as it can crowd your glassware and flatware. Maintaining these proportions ensures your tablescape feels organized and airy. It allows every design element to have its own breathing room. ### How do I clean a linen table runner after a holiday meal? Clean your linen runner by spot-treating spills immediately with a mild detergent. Most high-quality linens are machine-washable on a gentle cycle with cool water. Don't use bleach or harsh chemicals that can damage the fibers. You can air dry the runner or tumble dry it on low heat to achieve a soft, natural texture. Many hosts prefer the slightly lived-in look of unpressed linen for a relaxed yet sophisticated holiday vibe that feels approachable. ### Can I layer a table runner over a tablecloth? Layering a runner over a tablecloth is a brilliant way to add depth and dimension to your setting. This technique allows you to mix different textures, such as a crisp cotton tablecloth paired with a heavy linen runner. It provides a formal, curated look that feels intentional and professionally styled. Just ensure the colors complement each other to maintain aesthetic harmony. It's the perfect approach for creating a lush, multi-dimensional tablescape that truly impresses. ### What are the most popular colors for Thanksgiving 2026? Popular colors for 2026 move away from traditional orange toward "New Neutrals" like sage green, champagne, and muted charcoal. Sophisticated tablescapes also incorporate deep jewel tones like moody plum and burgundy for added drama. These earthy, warm tones reflect a shift toward a more organic and curated aesthetic. Using these hues in your thanksgiving table runners creates a modern foundation that pairs beautifully with natural greenery, acorns, and warm metallic accents. ### How do I choose a runner that matches my existing glassware? Match your runner to your glassware by coordinating colors or contrasting textures. If you have colored goblets or wine glasses, choose a runner in a neutral tone like charcoal or cream to make the glass pop. Alternatively, a runner with a subtle pattern can pull out specific hues from your glassware for a cohesive look. CNN Underscored associate home and gifts editor Nikol Slatinska had a blast testing the calendar with her mom, who similarly loves all things beauty. From a brightening Caudalíe eye cream to a lovely skin-scent perfume by Juliette Has A Gun, the items inside this gorgeous box are so exciting to discover. It’s almost impossible to believe you can get the entire calendar for under $100. ### Uncommon Goods 12 Days of Hot Sauce Advent Calendar It's surprisingly hard to find a good Advent calendar for hot sauce fans, as a lot of the options on the market lack flavor or are too vinegar-heavy. CNN Underscored home and gifts editor Amina Lake Patel recently tried and enjoyed this one from Uncommon Goods, which features 12 mini bottles of Torchbearer Sauces. Some of the included flavors were even featured on the show "Hot Ones," but Patel's favorite so far is the Psycho Curry. ### Tea Forté Volaré 12-Day Advent Calendar Slatinska tried two of Tea Forté’s Advent calendars last year, and for this year, she picked up the brand’s Volaré calendar, which features 12 tea flavors, including three new ones for 2026. Made in collaboration with the New York Botanical Garden, the calendar boasts a distinct, display-worthy design that’ll instantly dress up your tea or coffee bar. It’s the perfect cozy gift for any tea drinker in your life. Related article The 9 best tea kettles you can buy, according to editors and tea industry experts ### Vahdam Advent Calendar 2026 Vahdam’s Advent calendar has entered Slatinska’s daily tea rotation with its 24 diverse flavors. From Lychee Lemon to Hibiscus Licorice, the calendar provides an opportunity to try tea varieties most people probably wouldn’t pick up at their local supermarkets. For $20, the brand also has a this tea Advent calendar that arrives in a ready-to-hang folder. ### Voluspa 12-Day Alpine Advent Calendar Voluspa’s 2026 Advent calendar is pretty similar to last year’s, but that doesn’t make us any less excited for it. Inside, you’ll find 12 votive candles, each of which has a burn time of about 25 hours, in scents from the brand’s bestselling and holiday collections that we love (think Crushed Candy Cane, Forbidden Fig and White Cypress). Slatinska is a longtime fan of the brand and burns a new candle from this calendar in her home every week. The calendar also comes with a gold wick trimmer. Pro tip: Always trim wicks before each burn to make candles last longer! ### Craftspring Nutcracker Minis Advent Calendar Even if you don’t recognize this brand by its name, you’ve probably seen its adorable felted wool ornaments, which come in all kinds of styles for different occasions year-round. This one is Nutcracker-themed and comes with 24 of the small trinkets to hang on your tree and around your home. Patel received the calendar and said each ornament feels high-quality. “I love that they're handmade, which helps justify the price a bit,” she said. “I got the Nutcracker version because I love the classic ballet theme, but they all seem equally adorable. These ornaments would be perfect for kids or anyone with a mini Christmas tree!” ### Charlotte Tilbury Charlotte's Hollywood Beauty Wonderland Advent Calendar Multiple editors on our team are fans of Charlotte Tilbury’s makeup products, and this Advent calendar lets you try some of the brand's bestsellers in both full and travel sizes. That includes viral items from the Pillow Talk lip collection and complexion products that’ll leave your skin looking contoured and glowy. Plus, it all comes packaged in a dazzling red chest that any beauty aficionado would be thrilled to receive. Related article 50 premium beauty products from Amazon our editors can’t live without ### The Woobles Here We Go A-Wooblin' Advent Calendar Patel was gifted one of the beginner crochet kits from The Woobles a few years ago and found it to be the ideal meditative hobby for the winter. The brand's Advent calendar comes with four full-sized crochet kits and four accessory kits (complete with step-by-step videos), plus some exclusive collectibles, so you'll have plenty to do this holiday season. ### Fly By Jing 2026 Limited-Edition 12-Day Advent Calendar “Fly By Jing's pantry goods are staples in my household, so I was so excited to unbox this 12-day Advent calendar ahead of the holiday season,” Patel said. “Of course, you'll find an assortment of the brand's chili crisps, noodles (my favorite) and spices inside.” What makes this calendar an extra special buy is the fact that there are even some brand-new and discontinued products you won't find anywhere else. This year, the brand is also offering a 24-day calendar for those who want even more surprises, including ornaments and home goods. That said, we think the 12-day calendar will be more than enough for most people. ### L'Occitane Limited-Edition Advent Calendar Set L'Occitane makes our favorite hand cream, but as much as we love the French beauty brand, we’re willing to go out on a limb and say our readers enjoy its luxurious offerings even more than we do. Last holiday season, L'Occitane's gift sets were a major hit with our audience, and we’re certain this Advent calendar will be too. Featuring soaps, lotions and shower products in divine scents like Almond and Cherry Blossom, this calendar will delight anyone in need of some pampering this season. The brand also has a 12-day calendar you can shop at Sephora. ### Mystery Tackle Box 12 Days of Fishmas Advent Calendar Know any avid fishermen? Whether that’s your dad, grandpa or another member of your family, they’re bound to appreciate this hobby-themed Advent calendar. Inside, the recipient can open up boxes of fishing lures and decals that they can’t find anywhere else. ### See's Candies 2026 Advent Calendar Available now for preorder, See’s Candies limited-edition Advent calendar is just the thing to gift the chocolate lover on your list. Slatinksa has been enjoying some of the brand’s other giftable treats this season, including the gourmet lollipops and Scotchmallows, and she looks forward to indulging more once the calendar becomes available for shipping in November. Inside the adorable candy shop-themed box, you’ll uncover 24 delicious treats that’ll delight your taste buds, from butterscotch squares to a marshmallow tree. Related article The 25 best food gifts for people who take eating seriously ### Uncommon Goods Christmas Mystery Advent Calendar Uncommon Goods has a slew of unconventional Advent calendars that double as activities, like this mystery calendar. It’s a fun gift for the entire family because anyone above age 10 can participate in the escape room-style adventure, and up to five people can team up to solve the daily riddles. ### Lego Star Wars Advent Calendar 2026 Know any Star Wars fans? Anyone ages 6 and up can get in on the Lego fun while counting down the days until Christmas with this calendar. As you open the doors each day, you’ll get to put together beloved characters like the Mandalorian, iconic spacecraft like the Imperial Light Cruiser and more mini Star Wars-themed builds. Related article Lego’s newest Advent calendars include festive Star Wars, Marvel and Disney sets ### Vosges Haut-Chocolat 2026 Advent Calendar Vosges is known for its luxury chocolates, so this Advent calendar is exactly what you'd expect from the brand. The box displays a gorgeous winter lodge, complete with warm LED lights to round out the cozy scene. Patel tested last year's calendar and found it to be an incredibly enchanting experience. You can even reuse the lodge next year because the brand offers Advent calendar refills. Plus, each day comes with multiple pieces of chocolate for you to savor or share. ### Laithwaites 2026 Wine Advent Calendar This wine Advent calendar is something our managing editor Rachel Quigley tried last year and recommends to any wine lover. "I was absolutely thrilled when I saw the adorable holiday-themed box it comes in — so festive and whimsical," she said of last year's calendar. It comes with 24 different mini bottles of wine from all over the globe and even a bottle of prosecco to pop open on (spoiler alert) Dec. 24. You can preorder the calendar for $25 and pay the rest when it ships (for free). Related article 42 unique gifts to give (and get) in 2026, handpicked by our gift guide editor ### Walker's Shortbread Advent Calendar Patel was so excited to bring this Advent calendar home from work last year because her husband loves Walker’s Shortbread. "We ate a couple cookies on the couch (delicious as expected), but when I woke up the next morning, I was shocked to find out he had eaten the rest after I went to bed!" she said. "Hopefully you have more self-control around shortbread cookies than we do." ### Bokksu Luminous Japan Advent Calendar If their favorite part of traveling is getting to try new foods, this Advent calendar from Bokksu, the Japanese snack subscription service, will be right up their alley. This year’s version features a stunning paper lantern design, but it’s what’s inside that really counts. Slatinska has enjoyed trying the curated snacks, of which there are 32, as well as seven holiday collectibles that’ll temporarily transport them to a new place through different flavors. ### Nespresso x Swarovski Vertuo Advent Calendar Coffee Pack Shopping for someone who recently got a Nespresso Vertuo machine? Patel thinks this calendar, which comes with 24 capsules, including some from the holiday collection, is great for people who want to discover new coffees each day leading up to the holiday. You'll also find two biscuits and a surprise gift on the 24th day (and just a heads-up, it's not a Swarovski crystal). There's a version of the Nespresso Advent calendar for the Original line of machines too. ### Flaviar 2026 Whiskey Advent Calendar Mike Bruno, our VP of commerce, was seriously impressed with this whiskey Advent calendar when he tried it last year. "This is just the vibe I’m after around the holidays," he said. The calendar comes with 24 drams, as well as a booklet containing details on each one and room for tasting notes, plus a pair of Glencairn tasting glasses for proper sipping. The impressively varied selection will wow even the most seasoned whiskey connoisseur. ### Beekman 1802 The Kindness Café Advent Calendar We look forward to seeing Beekman 1802’s Advent calendar every year because the brand always impresses with its unique designs and generous product offerings. "One year, it included a bunch of mini-sized body creams that I saved and took with me on my travels that year, which was so handy," our fashion and beauty editor, Sophie Shaw, said. This year, half the calendar is filled with full-size products, so you can properly try many of Beekman’s bestselling goat milk skin and body care favorites. And because the 2026 calendar is café-themed, you also get a cute Barista Goatie collectible in your purchase. Related article The 36 best beauty Advent calendars to grab ahead of the holidays ### Papier 24-Day Advent Calendar Anyone who loves stationery will have a blast opening Papier's 24-day Advent calendar. Patel received last year’s version and said it was one of her favorites. “I love that everything comes gorgeously packaged in individual boxes rather than perforated cardboard, which makes opening up each day feel like a real treat,” she said, adding that she still uses items from last year’s calendar daily, including fancy rollerball pens, mini notebooks, paperclips and a pen pouch. “I ended up giving some of the products inside to my sister, who's a teacher, but I appreciate that the brand is offering a smaller, more affordable version this year too,” she said. ### Williams Sonoma Peppermint Bark Advent Calendar Patel has always had a love-hate relationship with minty chocolate, but Williams Sonoma’s Peppermint Bark is the real deal. This 24-day calendar comes with the beloved crunchy peppermint bark in four holiday-themed shapes, like snowmen and toy soldiers. She also got a taste of the brand's Peppermint Bark Flurries. "I’ll just say I really hope those make their way into an Advent calendar one day too," Patel added. ### Dandelion Chocolate 2026 Advent Calendar "I have a major sweet tooth, and this is hands down the best chocolate Advent calendar I’ve tried," Patel said. "Everything from the high-end packaging (each day’s box doubles as an ornament!) to the uniquely flavored chocolates inside screams luxury." What's more, you have the option to order a two-person version so each day has two pieces of chocolate. This makes it so much easier to share the experience with a loved one. Related article The 16 best Christmas ornament storage ideas, according to professional organizers ### In Good Taste 2026 Wine Advent Calendar Quigley gifts herself In Good Taste’s wine Advent calendar every year. She likes this version that comes with 24 6-ounce bottles of reds, whites and rosés, all crafted by the brand's in-house winemaker. And if you prefer just reds or just whites and rosés, In Good Taste has dedicated wine Advent calendars you'll enjoy too. Read our review ### Chris Loves Julia 3D Advent Calendar Most of the Advent calendars on the market are made of cardboard and get tossed after the holiday season is over. Consider buying a reusable Advent calendar — like this one with a 3D horse from design duo Chris Loves Julia — and filling it yourself year after year. You can even get it personalized with your family name for an extra $17. ### Compartés Winter Fox Chocolate Advent Calendar We’re big fans of Compartés chocolates here at CNN Underscored. The brand’s gourmet chocolate truffles have unique flavors that melt in your mouth, and this Advent calendar includes some limited-edition offerings that you won’t find anywhere else. The Crème Brûlée truffles are calling our names. ## How to choose the best Advent calendar Choosing an Advent calendar is as easy as picking one out that suits your (or the recipient’s) interests. If you’ve got a major sweet tooth, then you’ll probably be drawn to one of the chocolate or candy Advent calendars on this list. If you’re shopping for someone who’s looking to pick up a new screen-free hobby, a Woobles crochet kit Advent calendar might be the perfect gift they’d never think to get themselves. You should also look at whether the Advent calendar has 24 or 12 days’ worth of surprises so you can set your expectations. If you start your countdown on Dec. 1 but don’t have enough items to get you to Christmas Eve, you’ll probably be left disappointed. Similarly, it’s a good idea to consider the overall value of an Advent calendar. If you don’t care about spoilers, take a look at the list of products included and see how many are miniature versus full size. This will help you determine if the cost of the calendar is worth it to you. Even if you’re not getting the best deal out there, an Advent calendar could be worth buying because of the novelty factor. ## FAQs ### What is an Advent calendar used for? Advent calendars are designed to count down the days until Christmas, so they typically have 24 or 25 openings filled with treats or small surprises. In that case, you’d open the first one on Dec. 1 so you can spread the holiday cheer throughout the beginning of the month. Other Advent calendars have only 12 days (for the 12 days of Christmas), which means you open the first door on Christmas Day. However, some people choose to start those 12-day countdowns on Dec. 13 instead. We’ve done it both ways, so the choice is yours! ### What can you put inside a DIY Advent calendar? You can put in anything that fits inside the Advent calendar’s drawers or boxes, so the options are practically endless. Here are some ideas to get you started. ## Why trust CNN Underscored CNN Underscored’s editors carefully curate each gift guide to include a selection of products tailored to the person you’re shopping for. Gift ideas in this guide include products hand-tested by our team, foolproof presents we’ve given (or have been given) ourselves, new products from our favorite brands and trending items taking over our social feeds. Our aim is to inspire you to gift creatively by presenting you with gifts you may not have seen or considered (but if you’re seeing some repeat products in our guides, it probably just means we really love them). For this article, CNN Underscored home and gifts editor Amina Lake Patel and associate home and gifts editor Nikol Slatinska rounded up the best Advent calendars for the 2026 holiday season they’ve seen so far. Amina Lake Patel (formerly Abdelrahman) is the home and gifts editor for CNN Underscored, where she oversees both verticals and works with a team of writers. When she’s not at work, you can find her taking long walks outside, bingeing “Grey’s Anatomy” or trying to snuggle with her cat, Tango. ### Latest Articles Nikol Slatinska is the associate home & gifts editor for CNN Underscored. She is based in New York City. Her writing focuses on furniture, home decor, small appliances, cleaning and organizing. ### Latest Articles ### Explore trending products ### Inna Olshansky Ceramic Purple and Blue Dreidel and Stand ### Ess-a-Bagel New York Bagel Brunch for Six ### Pottery Barn Hanukkah Medallion Lazy Susan ### FarmSteady Jelly Donut-Making Kit ### More recommendations *Note: The prices above reflect the retailers' listed price at the time of publication.* ### Deal of the Day © 2026 Cable News Network. web_sources.page_content: By Mari Uyehara and Samantha Schoech Advent calendars began as a Christian tradition in the 19th century and have grown to be part of secular holiday fun as well. In the weeks leading up to Christmas, they provide a daily delight. We tested and tasted our way through a bunch of Advent calendars (somebody had to) and gathered some of our favorites for kids and adults, including an annually anticipated beauty calendar, our favorite Lego versions, a spicy sauce and snack collection, and many more. Many of our picks are from companies and makers that we have already vetted in their respective categories. Check out the best teas we’ve tasted, the best boxed chocolates, and the best Lego sets for kids for year-round excellence. ## Edible (and drinkable) calendars ### Bokksu Advent Calendar The 24 drawers in this gorgeously made Advent calendar hold a world of Japanese treasures: 17 kinds of sweets and snacks, plus seven little collectibles. A legit stunner, the Bokksu Luminous Japan Advent Calendar is revealed when you open two doors with translucent blue window panels sandwiched by paper lantern cutouts. In 17 of the 24 drawers are delectable treats, many of them multiple: matcha KitKats, orange gummies, hojicha chocolate crunch, savory crackers, and more. And the remaining seven contain things you can (and will want to) keep — a patterned cloth, a small ceramic piece, and so forth. We had assumed that this pricey, sophisticated set might appeal most to adults, but when we let one Japanophile tween at it, he tore through every single box in near ecstasy, which convinced us that it’s a winner for families, as well. Though we still recommend opening one drawer daily, we can report that, unlike many Advent calendars, the Bokksu version contains unique surprises that don’t get repetitive and continue to thrill right to the last one. ### Murray’s Cheese Countdown Calendar The New York–based cheese company showcases 12 days of crowd-pleasing dairy delights and accoutrements, such as fruit spreads and crackers, in an adorably illustrated box. A savory counterpoint to legions of sweet Advent calendars, the 12 Days Of Murray’s Cheese Countdown Calendar has plenty of good stuff for those who choose the cheese plate over dessert. At first glance, our kitchen team thought the selections could be more deep-cut, but once they started tasting, they were surprised by how good many of the crowd-pleasing classics were and how much they enjoyed them. Take the pepper jack: Normally a simple supermarket offering, the Murray’s version was extra creamy with a pervasively verdant jalapeño flavor and a lovely, sweet finish. “I’m still thinking about that one,” admitted kitchen editor and new convert Marilyn Ong. “I was really taken aback by its deliciousness.” Just note: The calendar does sell out each year, and since the box contains perishable products, it ships with ice packs and must be refrigerated upon arrival. ### See’s Candies Advent Calendar See’s Chocolates are a California institution, and this many-drawered Advent calendar gives candy lovers far and wide a chance to sample 24 different treats, including the company’s famed lollipops. “This 102-year-old company nails delicious nostalgia, especially at the holidays. Though if you’re Californian, I probably don’t need to sell you on the appeal of digging through one of See’s famous assortment boxes for dark chocolate scotchmallows,” said writer Rachel Wharton. See’s Candies doesn’t use any preservatives in its confections, so you know each bite is going to be fresh and delicious. We love the mix of foil-wrapped solid milk chocolates, filled chocolates, and its famous lollipops, all of which are included in the snowy brick-facade setting of this calendar. ### Fly By Jing Advent Calendar The 12-day Advent calendar contains a surprise collection of 2-ounce jars of condiments, spices, and sauces, plus noodles and snacks, all inspired by the flavors of Sichuan and all vegan. The 12-day Fly By Jing 2026 Advent Calendar offers a chance to taste a dozen tingly products inspired by China’s Sichuan province. This year’s selection includes some of the company’s best-selling chili crisps, as well as noodles, a hot sauce, and a new hot honey (“really yummy,” according to our kitchen team). One bummer from our testing this year: The included ornament was broken when we opened it. And be sure to order early — last year the limited-edition calendar sold out by November 15. ### Bonne Maman Advent Calendar 2026 Edition The 24 doors in Bonne Maman’s Advent calendar house classic (four fruits, mixed berry) and exclusive spreads, jams, and honeys in darling mini jars. Why not spread the love? Get a Bonne Maman Advent Calendar for yourself, and send others to friends and family. When the 24 adorably tiny jars are empty, you can use them to save leftover condiments, bring spices on a camping trip, display a single flower bud, store leftover paint and sequins, or stock a play kitchen. ### Adagio Teas Advent Calendar Available in versions with loose tea or tea bags, this Adagio calendar offers novel, yuletide blends for each day leading up to Christmas. The tea obsessives on our staff have sung the praises of family-owned Adagio Teas’s Silver Needle white tea in our best teas guide. And the Adagio Teas Nutcracker Advent Calendar gives heavy tea drinkers and casual sippers alike a chance to try new holiday flavors, such as Pomegranate Grove and Candy Cane. The calendar comes in loose-leaf, tea-bag, and decaf versions, and there are clear directions (with brew temp and time) right on the package, so you don’t ruin your cuppa. ### McCrea’s Caramel 2026 Advent Calendar Behind each paper-flapped door, revelers will find one of 12 flavors of gourmet caramel from the famed Massachusetts confectioner. The world of caramels involves more than just butter and sugar. To offer more variety to those with a sweet tooth, the McCrea’s Caramel Advent Calendar packs a dozen different flavors of caramel behind its 24 doors. The flavors range from the traditional Classic Vanilla, Chocolate Orange, Christmas Plum, and Gingerbread to the intriguing Black Lava Sea Salt, so you’ll have plenty of opportunity to pick a favorite. And this year’s packaging features dreamy artwork of a kitty family by Boston-based artist Angellize Rivera. ### La Boîte à Bonbons 2026 Advent Calendar These soft gummy candies from Montreal are fresh and perfectly chewy, and they taste like fruit rather than artificial flavoring. Canadian candy company La Boîte à Bonbons makes perfectly chewy and pillowy gummies in surprisingly authentic fruit flavors. Each pull-out box in the La Boîte à Bonbons 2026 Advent Calendar contains three to six pieces of sweet or sour soft candies. It’s an unusually generous little handful of berries, worms, fruits, and rings. The numbers of calendars are limited, and this year’s version is likely to sell out. You can order immediately and choose your delivery week from a drop-down menu. ### Dandelion Chocolate 2026 Advent Calendar These exquisite Advent calendars are designed by a different artist every year. Inside cylindrical boxes are Dandelion chocolate confections reimagined by 25 different chocolatiers. The Dandelion Chocolate Advent Calendar from this San Francisco–based bean-to-bar chocolate maker is pricey but absolutely stunning. Each little cylinder-shaped box nestled inside doubles as an ornament and contains a confection from a different chocolatier from across North America and Japan, using Dandelion’s chocolate. The selection ranges from ganaches to caramels to candied citrus, and every one is special. “I think it’s worth the price just to sample chocolates from so many great chocolatiers,” said editorial director Marguerite Preston, “but the boxes are also so sturdy and beautiful that you could totally reuse them to make your own Advent calendar in years to come.” And if sharing is just too big an ask, Dandelion also makes a double-portion Advent calendar for two. ### Flaviar Whiskey Advent Calendar 2026 This box includes 24 unlabeled whiskey nips from the world at large alongside two shapely tasting glasses. There’s also a link to an app that asks sippers to rate the day’s sample before revealing its origins. Wirecutter writer and bourbon fan Thom Dunn has tried a lot of whiskey Advent calendars in his day, but the Flaviar Whiskey Advent Calendar stands out because “it actually sort of teaches you about whiskey.” Each of the 24 mystery bottles, 50 mL in size, is numbered but otherwise nondescript. Tasters sip the day’s whiskey and then rate it on a proprietary app that reveals full details. There’s always at least one very pricey whiskey in the batch, and it’s fun looking back to see how you rated it blindly, compared with your ratings for, say, Jim Beam. Beware: It always sells out. ## Calendars for adults and teens ### Clue Advent Calendar Each door of this 24-day murder-mystery Advent calendar contains a puzzle to solve, which leads to the door with the next clue. The puzzles take about five to 10 minutes to complete. If your family revels in solving puzzles together, the engrossing Clue Advent Calendar is a real ride. At the Tudor Mansion on a snowy winter night, six guests arrive at the invitation of their wealthy host, Boddy Black, who is subsequently murdered. To solve this whodunit, the group reads a short story and opens one door to a new puzzle for each of the 24 days. One day might involve using logical deduction to decipher a recipe, while another might ask you to put together a pattern and match it to a door. To find the next door (they are unnumbered), the group needs to solve the day’s puzzle, but there are three hints if you get stumped. We looked forward to the bonding activity every night and had a blast figuring out each brainteaser together. ### Revolve Beauty Advent Calendar This collection of best-selling products, packed in a sturdy mini suitcase, includes 10 full-size finds alongside a selection of generous minis in a rare beauty Advent calendar bargain. You’d be hard-pressed to find a better value for a beauty obsessive than the Revolve Beauty Advent Calendar, which pairs 13 full-size best-selling products alongside minis and accessories, with an estimated value of over $950. Highlights include Summer Fridays Dream Lip Oil, Ilia Base Face Milk, Benefit Benetint Lip & Cheek Stain, and Babe Original Essential Lash Serum. There are also hair products, beauty accessories, and wellness gummies. It’s all packaged up in a pink and red, metal-handled suitcase that you could use to store your new loot year-round. Revolve Beauty also sells a 12-day Advent calendar set. ### Anthropologie Beauty Advent Calendar Packed in an illustrated maroon-hued box, this set includes premium samples, among them Sunday Riley Good Genes, Salt & Stone Santal & Vetiver Deodorant, and Phlur Missing Persons Eau de Parfum. Beauty Advent calendars abound, but the Anthropologie The 24 Days of Beauty Advent Calendar, fancifully illustrated in maroons and pinks by London-based illustrator Nephthys Foster, is particularly beautiful. Unlike the Revolve calendar, it contains only large samples — not full sizes — but that may be preferable for those who prefer to test before committing any vanity space. The wide-ranging assortment includes scents, skin and hair care, nail products, and makeup. And it features products that may appeal to both Gen Z (Phlur Missing Person fragrance, Celebritips press-on nails) and their parents (Sunday Riley Good Genes, Salt & Stone deodorant). There’s also a 12-day version with a different set of products, including L’Occitane Almond Shower Oil and OPI Funny Bunny Nail Lacquer, for about half the price, but we prefer the assortment in the larger version. ### The McSweeney’s Advent Calendar A knee-slapper for the erudite, this boxed set includes 24 mini holiday-humor books from the catalog of indie publisher McSweeney’s. It had us literally laughing out loud. It’s not just the look of The McSweeney's Advent Calendar that we love; it’s the personality. Designed as a diminutive boxed set with illustrations by Sophy Hollington, it contains 24 numbered mini hardback books. Each book is a standalone piece of holiday-adjacent humor writing, comics, letters, poetry, and more from the McSweeney’s world of books, magazines, and online literary publications. This year includes “Isaac Chotiner Interviews Santa Claus,” “Scenes from a Hallmark Hanukkah Movie,” and “Three Kings White Elephant Gift Exchange.” It’s not dirt cheap, but we can’t think of a better way to ring in the season than with beautiful design and a daily guffaw. There are only so many in print, and like almost everything McSweeney’s publishes, it’s sure to become a collector’s item. ### The Met Museum Favorites Advent Countdown Each magnetic mini puzzle in this Advent calendar features a beloved piece of art from The Met. Each of the 24 mini magnetic puzzles in The Met Museum Favorites Advent Countdown features an image of a Met classic. Open the flap doors to reveal a tiny paper bag containing the pieces. It might be Leutze’s “Washington Crossing the Delaware,” “The Great Wave off Kanagawa,” a Grecian urn, or Rodin’s “The Thinker.” Each puzzle is about 3 inches when finished. We only wish it included some information about the featured artwork. Note too that if you’ve bought The Met’s puzzle Advent calendar before, this is the same as 2025’s version. ### L’Occitane Beauty Advent Calendars In this box the high-end Provençal company features 24 days’ worth of beloved beauty classics, including Almond Shower Oil and Shea Butter Hand Cream. Choose from two versions: the more expensive Prestige and the slightly less expensive Classic. A classic favorite, the L’Occitane Beauty Advent Calendars are highly anticipated every year. Among the many Advent calendars that beauty and personal-care writer Neha Tandon has tested, she says, the luxurious L’Occitane Prestige Advent Calendar seems to be the one that’s really worth its price. “I kept all my favorites and then added the rest onto bigger gifts for loved ones,” she attested. Among her long list of keepers, Neha cited the Immortelle Divine Cream, Overnight Oil Serum, and Amande Sublime Exfoliating Soap. The 24-product sampler features 13 deluxe sizes and a full-size Almond Shower Oil. There’s also a slightly less expensive L’Occitane Classic Advent Calendar, which features less than half as many deluxe versions and no full sizes. ## Kids calendars ### Bluey Advent Calendar Fans of the dog-family animation series won’t be disappointed with this 24-day Advent calendar, which we think is a great deal for this many “Bluey” figurines. “What a dream!” enthused editor Signe Brewster, whose 5-year-old and 3-year-old gasped as they opened each door of the Bluey Advent Calendar 2026. Fans of the über-popular Australian animated series are treated to 24 surprises, and Signe reports that the figurines, in particular, are nice, heavyweight, and not destined for the trash. She does note that only her 5-year-old could open the cardboard doors without help, but we consider that a sign of the calendar’s strong construction compared with those that ripped too easily. The only real dings, according to Signe’s children, were that they were confused as to why there were no figurines of the parents, and the stickers were disappointing compared with everything else. But overall, “the girls had a ton of fun with this and are happily playing with the pieces now.” ### National Geographic Mega Science Advent Calendar Mini experiments, rocks, and fossils provide the perfect, project-based lead-up to Christmas for budding scientists. It seems like nearly every kid goes through the collecting rocks, crystals, and fossils stage, and for them, we love the boredom-curing Mega Science Advent Calendar. (Bonus points for not being candy, which we’re sure they’ll get plenty of over the season.) It contains 13 easy experiments to make a test tube glow, grow crystals, and float coins, plus 11 treasure-worthy rocks and fossils. But before they even reach December 1, they get to open the protective goggles. Safety first! It’s recommended for kids 8 to 12, and it could be fun as a family project. ### The Woobles Here We Go A-Wooblin’ Advent Calendar This set contains four kid-friendly crochet projects for crafting roly-poly animals. Instructions are available via a handy QR code. Our kids team loves the easy, beginner-friendly crochet kits from The Woobles and calls them “virtually idiot-proof.” The Woobles Here We Go A-Wooblin’ Advent Calendar contains four full-size crochet kits, mini projects, and a bunch of hooks, plus crochet accessories, all in cute Christmas-themed boxes tucked into a fold-out-case workshop. Each Woobles kit comes with a QR code for access to video instructions. ### Lego Advent calendars The 31-piece comic-themed calendar includes festive accessories mixed in with favorite superheroes, such as Captain America wielding a candy cane and Iron Man’s gift-wrapping robot. Disney Princess fans ages 5 years and over will be thrilled by this building set that features Moana, Mulan, Ariel, and more. With seven mini-build vehicles and iconic characters in festive dress, this Mandalorian-themed Advent calendar offers family bonding for fans ages 6 and older. Just look at Grogu in his adorable red holiday sweater. Wirecutter’s staff includes many AFOLs (adult fans of Lego), as well as fans of Lego’s sets for kids. We can quibble about the various merits of individual minifigures or set-design creativity, but we love the Lego Advent calendars because they offer one mini build a day — for adults and kids alike. The build instructions are on the back of the little doors. Editor Hannah Morrill’s 4-year-old son enjoyed the uniqueness of each build — a plane, a helicopter, a launcher — even if they did require a little help with assembly. (Kids even one year older would be fine.) ### Mini Brands Advent Calendar A little on the pricey side, this 24-day Advent calendar delivers faux food, characters, and more to devotees of the small-scale collectibles. For many parents, the Mini Brands franchise seems like a cheery assault on the environment, with its parade of wasteful plastic orbs. And that’s part of why we love the Mini Brands Advent Calendar so much. Instead of plastic balls destined for landfills, the calendar delivers adorable minuscule faux food, characters, and other teeny toys. Gifts editor Hannah Morrill’s 8-year-old daughter was thrilled with it. “She says she feels like a YouTube influencer that has all the Mini Brands stuff,” reported Hannah. We only wish it were about half the price. If your mini is mad for minis, this box may scratch the itch for good. ### Playmobil Advent calendars Collect a winter wonderland of horses, a barn, a sleigh, and other animals with this 24-day advent calendar. This 84-piece set supplies everything needed to create a European Christmas market, including ice skaters and a booth selling sweets. Playmobil’s various Advent calendars, marketed for children ages 4 to 10 years old, are always a hit. The Playmobil Advent Calendar Christmas Sleigh Ride is geared toward animal lovers, with a waterfall backdrop and 24 figurines, including a barn, horse, and dog. And the Christmas Market Advent Calendar, with its ice skating rink and holiday treats, seems inspired by Germanic Christmas markets. After the kids collect the daily figurines, the payoff on Christmas morning is a gift in itself — a tableau of trinkets they’ll love to play with all year long. “My brother and I would dutifully take turns with who got to open up the paper window every day during December,” said Wirecutter’s Kelsey Dang. “The attention to detail in the accessories is delightful, and the goal of building out a full scene keeps the suspense going throughout the month.” ## Do-it-yourself Advent calendar If your favorite Advent calendar is sold out for the season, or you can’t find one that fits your fancy, you can always make your own — with a little help. Customizing and filling a reusable, blank calendar can become a new tradition you’ll look forward to for years to come. Many craft stores sell unpainted, preassembled wooden Advent calendars that you can decorate yourself. Finished versions like this simple graphic drawer-style calendar abound, as do hanging cloth calendars from the traditional to the understated. (We’re also tempted to try a nightly beer or canned cocktail with this $70 Wisconsin-made tree calendar designed to hold cans.) Once you’ve got your vessel, it’s on to the fun part of filling it. The makers of some of Wirecutter’s most beloved teas, such as Fortnum & Mason and Kusmi Tea, sell sampler packs, as does scented-candle maker Keap, so you can pop a few into your calendar pockets. We also suggest many small gifts in our guides to stocking stuffers for kids and adults. Other ideas include mini art supplies, socks, hair accessories, lip balm, seed packets, tinned fish, and soaps. Just make sure to take measurements of the drawers or pockets on your calendar before you start shopping for trinkets. If you prefer something sweet, one of our favorite boxes of chocolate, Melissa Coppel Bonbons, contains 24 colorful pieces — just enough to last until Christmas, if your giftee can wait that long. On the other hand, if you get two boxes of our top pick from Recchiuti Confections, you’ll have eight pieces left over for snacking. Either way, be sure to store your choco-fabulous Advent calendar in a cool, dry environment. This article was edited by Hannah Morrill and Jennifer Hunter. ## Meet your guides Mari Uyehara I cover a wide range of gift giving, with a specialty in food and drink gifts; I also touch on beauty on occasion. I work to ensure that we consider a diverse range of socio-cultural backgrounds in our guides. Samantha Schoech I discover, vet, and write about gifts of all kinds from my office in San Francisco. I am particularly drawn to all things shiny or bookish, but I try not to impose my taste more than is strictly necessary. ## Mentioned above * From iced herbal teas to strong black brews, here are the best teas according to Wirecutter’s obsessive staff.The Best Teas We’ve Tasted * Our kid testers, and their parents, loved these Lego sets.The Best Lego Sets for Kids * We wielded hundreds of wands and sweated through dozens of formulations to find the best mascaras for every eye shape and lash type. These stylish, easy-to-learn craft kits will keep your hands busy.The Best Fiber Craft Kits for Adults * From a van Gogh piece to a retro radio, these are our favorite Lego sets for adults.The Best Lego Sets for Adults, According to Our Staff * We’ve tasted over 40 canned cocktails to find the best ones for all of your drinking, partying, and picnicking needs.The Best Canned Cocktails ## Further reading * ### Wirecutter’s 100 Most Popular Gifts Ever by Wirecutter Staff We recommend hundreds of gifts for every occasion, from celebrations to condolences to just because. Here are our top 100 most popular presents. * ### The 100 New Gifts We’re Most Excited About This Year by Sri Rain Stewart We’ve rounded up 100 of our favorite new gifts from 2025, ranging from timeless home finds to indulgent skin care, hobbyist essentials, and more. * ### The Most Popular Wirecutter-Approved Gifts of 2025 by Sri Rain Stewart and Sarah Gannett These 100 items are the most-purchased Wirecutter gifts so far this year. * ### Look No Further. limitations: Google Trends indices measure relative searches, not Amazon traffic or units sold.
Each term uses a separate fixed-window scale. Compare timing within a keyword; do not compare index magnitudes as demand size.
Monthly averages approximate source indices by overlapping days; historical peak is within selected months only.
Future months beyond the as-of date are blank, not zero. A completed current-year period can contribute to timing.
Amazon prices, purchase bands and ratings are current snapshots, not historical monthly ASIN sales.
A top-five list is a transparent shortlist within this limited sample, not Amazon's global top five or a sales forecast.
Review publication month is not verified purchase month. Reviews may share variants and do not establish US demographics.
Full reviews and linked review excerpts are counted separately. Excerpts without date or rating remain undated/unrated; AI summaries are excluded. Records are not necessarily unique customers.
Purchase evidence preserves exact ASIN, source type and observation date. Search-result badges supplement coverage but do not silently replace product-page snapshots or enter Top 5 ranking.
Search sampling is not comprehensive market coverage. Missing review/source data does not imply low demand or low competition.
Configured families are survey seeds, not proof they are hot. No profit estimate is made without costs.
